reconcile.connective: Defenders distinguish two Horites named Dishon — a son of Seir and a grandson through Anah — so the lists describe different men, not one father.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells' Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the Genesis 36 list as self-contradictory, since the text names Dishon a son of Seir and also a child of Anah.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999), contra/anah.html

excerpts.author: John Gill
excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: And these are the sons of Dishon,…. Not of Dishon the son of Anah, but of Dishon the son of Seir
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the tension by distinguishing two men named Dishon — son of Seir versus son of Anah — which dissolves the grandfather/father conflict.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Genesis 36:22
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill distinguishes Dishon son of Seir from Dishon son of Anah in this very list, the harmonization keyed directly to the passage.
